Triage: routed `domain:skills`. Rationale over the devx alternative the filer offered: the check guards the PM partial-delivery protocol, its predicate is exported from the pm tooling family (`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`), and the parent investigation (#8293) plus the adjacent gate-tooling cards (#8478, #8434) all live in the skills lane — keeping the family in one lane beats splitting by wiring location. The scope's step 1 (settle the fenced-code reading with one live probe) is correctly ordered first and is cheap.

Two flags for the record, both already in the card: ① **maintainer veto window** — this adds a blocking gate that touches every contributor; it stays in the round report until dispatched, veto by comment; ② serial constraints — after the H7 report-only PR merges (predicate export) and after the dispatch-gates self-test wiring card establishes the CI convention.

**Addendum — patch round on PR #8527. New head `2fe178e3737653e969deb0046bf8382eafa28b33` (fast-forward from `164d349`). The guard job is GREEN.**

## The fix, and why the first diagnosis pointed at the wrong step

The dispatch read the failure as "the job invokes pnpm (directly or via a setup step)" and offered mirroring the model workflow's install steps, or switching the invocation to plain `node`. Neither applied as framed, and the reason is the interesting part:

- The invocation was **already** plain `node scripts/check-partof-closing-keyword.mjs`. No `pnpm`, no `corepack`, anywhere in the workflow source.
- The model workflow (Duplicate Fix Guard) uses **neither setup-node nor pnpm** — it is a pure `actions/github-script` job. It has no install recipe to mirror.

The job log names the real culprit, and it is a step whose source mentions no package manager at all:

```
##[group]Run actions/setup-node@v5
with:
  node-version-file: .nvmrc
  package-manager-cache: true      <-- v5 input default
Resolved .nvmrc as 22
Found in cache @ /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/22.23.2/x64
##[error]Unable to locate executable file: pnpm.
```

`actions/setup-node@v5` defaults `package-manager-cache: true`, reads `packageManager: pnpm@…` out of package.json, and shells out to `pnpm` to locate the store it would cache. This job installs no package manager on purpose, so pnpm is not on PATH and the action hard-errors — **in `Setup Node.js`, before the script ever ran**. That is why no reading of the `run:` line could have found it.

**Fix:** matched the repo's own known-good recipe exactly. `adr-merge-approval.yml` is the precise precedent — checkout, `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version: '22'`, one `node scripts/check-*.mjs` call, no install and no corepack — and it was already concluding **success** on this very PR's head, which is what made it the measured choice rather than a guess. Every other setup-node in this repo is `@v7`; mine was the only `@v5`.

**Regression pin:** a new self-test case asserts the guard workflow names no package manager in any executable line (comments are stripped first, so the comment explaining this incident may say the word). Reverse-verified: reintroducing `pnpm exec` into the `run:` line reddens exactly that one case, 1 of 28.

## Green readings — two independent ones, both on `2fe178e`

| run | trigger | job conclusion | duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [31726646030](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/31726646030/job/94536557357) | `synchronize` (the push) | **success** | 8s |
| [31726767670](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/31726767670/job/94536967333) | `edited` (the PR-body update) | **success** | 9s |

Every step green in both, `Setup Node.js` included. The judging step's actual output, from the first run's log — the gate reading its own PR through the real event payload:

```
2026-08-13T17:37:46.3147970Z ✓ check:partof-closing-keyword: PR #8527 carries no Part-of/closing-keyword contradiction.
```

The second run is an unplanned but welcome bonus: updating the PR body **fired the `edited` trigger**, which is exactly the load-bearing property claimed for this wiring (without it, an author who reworded a flagged sentence could never go green, since a re-run replays the frozen payload). That path is now demonstrated live rather than argued.

## Re-verification after the patch

- New gate self-test: **28 cases green** (was 27; +1 package-manager pin).
- Gates re-derived against the patch's actual changed paths and run as a union — all green: `check:node-version` (the gate that governs setup-node spellings, and the one most likely to object to this change), `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:required-contexts`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:partof-closing-keyword`, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, `node scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs`, plus eslint on the changed script.
- PR body's Wiring section updated to describe what shipped, and a "Patch round" section records the failure and its cause.
- Worktree removed unforced; nothing left running.

Nothing in the predicate, the judging layer or the fence measurement changed in this round — the defect was entirely in the runtime step, which is also why the first head's red said nothing about the gate's correctness.

**Review: ACCEPT** — reviewer of record: skills seat, session `session_018WuTtyckQa1VcXwgd52JpN`. PR #8527 (final head `2fe178e`) reviewed across both rounds; the guard is green **on its own PR, twice, through the real event payload** — including an unplanned live demonstration of the `edited` trigger doing exactly the load-bearing job the wiring argument claimed for it.

- **Step 1 (fence reading)**: settled with a three-arm controlled probe — fences do NOT fire; closing links exist at PR-open time. The positive-control arm is what made the nulls interpretable; the one deviation from the dispatch sketch (a third throwaway target) bought exactly that and is endorsed. All four throwaway artifacts closed; measurement recorded beside the inline-span reading it extends.
- **Step 2 (the gate)**: predicate imported, not forked (the delegation ablation proves it — and the dev correctly noted its limit: delegation proves no-fork, only the fence case proves the rule); H1–H6 untouched report-only; per-number binding keeps correct `Part of A + Fixes B` PRs green; body via `env:`, no API read in the judging path; the three-way error split (1 / 2-NOT-WIRED / 0-with-witness) is the right honesty shape.
- **The patch round is a model incident writeup**: the live red was a failure in a tool the workflow's source never mentions — `actions/setup-node@v5`'s `package-manager-cache: true` default reading `packageManager` from package.json and shelling out to pnpm inside Setup Node, before any `run:` line. Fixed against the repo's real precedent for dependency-free node gates (`adr-merge-approval.yml`, setup-node@v7 — measured as already green on this very PR), with a regression pin so a package-manager reference in an executable line reddens the self-test.
- **On the record, three dispatch-level claims of mine were falsified by this dev's measurement**: ① "the watch-hint scan now masks comments/self-tests" — premature at dispatch time (the masking PR merged 20 minutes later); the dev's replacement mechanism (hints must be single unbroken tokens) is the correct standing reason fixture strings are safe; ② my patch-round diagnosis ("the job invokes pnpm directly or via a setup step") — it invoked neither; ③ my "mirror the Duplicate Fix Guard recipe" suggestion — that guard is a github-script job with no recipe for this shape. The corrections are better than the claims; this is the falsification channel working as designed.
- **Open question ruled (seat)**: option **A** — the gate stays a blocking-but-not-required check run. B is excluded by mechanism, not appetite: registry rule 6 requires queue-build reporting and a `merge_group` event carries no PR body; a registered entry would wedge the queue. If the maintainer ever wants it required, that is a Rulesets settings write only a human can make, noted in the round report.

**Landing**: normal queue path, `skip-changeset`. Heavy carriers on `2fe178e` still converging at review time — ready-flip + auto-merge fires on their `completed: success` (flip check armed). Precedent note for the next dependency-free `node scripts/check-*.mjs` gate: `adr-merge-approval.yml` is the named in-repo model — recorded for the CI-wiring card that follows this file family.
